title: I'm NOT a game developer, but I've always dreamed of making a game. Here's my progress so far with Opus 5.5
author: Tomtanks88
selftext:
I've always been passionate about gaming, and for the longest time, I've wanted to build a game of my own.

The only problem? I have absolutely no background in game development or coding.

So I decided to see how far I could get with AI helping me along the way.

This is a little look at the development stages of a story I've always wanted to tell through a game I've been experimenting with in Unity. From early environments and rough concepts to slowly bringing the world to life.

It's still very early, and there's a LOT that needs fixing, improving, and figuring out. But seeing something that started as an idea in my head slowly become something I can actually walk around in has been incredibly exciting.

I'm not trying to pretend I've suddenly become a game developer. I'm learning as I go, making mistakes, and using AI to help bridge the gaps in my knowledge.

Just wanted to share something I'm genuinely passionate about.

Would love to hear your thoughts!

comments.author: sillyandstrange
comments.body: It's inspiring, I'm in the same boat. How are you liking opus? I currently only have a 20 dollar plus sub for GPT, and codex has been alright, but I'm hearing such great things with opus.

replies.body:

I worked on the first slice (5 minutes of gameplay) and want to make it playable without issues before moving on to the next slice.   
Im trying to work on the animation and how the cloth simulate on the character but I find it extremely difficult and giving me really hard times.

comments.author: Cpt_Tripps
comments.body:
I suggest posting your AI workflow.

Adding features is incredibly easy with AI.

Getting advice about version control, workflow, and prompting will help you improve much faster.

replies.author: Tomtanks88
replies.body:
How can I do that? This is the first time I do this. If you have an example I would be happy to do it. 

Im already facing an issue with player character movement and cloth simulation. So I need all the help I can get.

replies.author: Cpt_Tripps
replies.body:
> Im already facing an issue with player character movement

So there are a few ways you can do character movement. The different options require different camera movements and different control schemes. AI tends to mix and match incorrectly.

replies.author: Cpt_Tripps
replies.body:
1st and 3rd person are the main differences but there are little variances.

Is turn speed a mechanic or can your character do 360's as quickly as a player can move their mouse.

Does A and D turn your character or make them crab walk sideways.

Does your character move/rotate when you are just looking at things on the screen?

Its kind of hard to describe you just need to play a game with a movement style you like and really analyze what is happening with the character, the animators, and the camera.

replies.author: Diabetus97
replies.body: That makes a lot of sense! Basic movements seem to be decent, but when I had codex try to make a sword swing animation, even after 3 passes with sol the sword was still clipping through the character and the arm rotation would’ve torn a rotator cuff twice. Tripo has a decent animation but I haven’t found anything super robust.

replies.author: Cpt_Tripps
replies.body:
Yeah AI really struggles to make things look good.

Swords in video games are just an issue because fully swinging through should be a kill which is fine for a lightsaber or a super powerful 1 hit weapon. Animating swords bouncing off players, shields, or items is incredibly time consuming. Most games just avoid it.
